section_summary: This section follows Peruvian and U.S. efforts to deport Abe Kenso and two associates accused of organizing and intimidating Japanese residents who accepted Japan’s defeat. It includes threatening letters, Abe’s public claims of an official mission, police and FBI reports, and records of the men’s transfer from Peru to U.S. custody. Documents from 1949 examine three Japanese associations in Peru and include their membership lists, correspondence, and statutes.

subfiles.title: Report on Japanese nationalist organizers and threatening letters
subfiles.about: Peruvian police arrests and anonymous threats against Japanese residents who accepted Japan’s defeat.
subfiles.summary: The report lists Japanese residents connected with a founding committee in Huancayo and describes arrests and expulsion decrees. It attributes threatening letters to Kenichiro Shimabukuro and others, then reproduces a letter denouncing its recipients as traitors and threatening their deaths.

subfiles.title: Airgram A-161 seeking information on Abe Kenso
subfiles.about: Requests verification of Abe’s claimed naval rank and mission from Emperor Hirohito.
subfiles.summary: Asks Tokyo to check Abe’s claims of being a rear admiral and imperial envoy.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 623 on Abe’s claims
subfiles.about: Reports Abe’s prison interview and request for an audience with Peru’s president.
subfiles.summary: Abe claimed to be a rear admiral and Hirohito’s envoy; he disputed the charges and impending deportation.

subfiles.title: Telegram on repatriation costs, concluding page
subfiles.about: Gives the estimated cost of transporting three Japanese deportees.
subfiles.summary: Estimates costs at $2,000–$2,500 and urges a Peruvian guarantee.

subfiles.title: Lima telegram on unpaid deportation costs
subfiles.about: Warns that Peru may release the three organizers across its border if transport cannot be arranged.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy reports Peru has not agreed to pay and urges guarded deportation.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on deporting three Japanese nationals
subfiles.to: Mr. León and Jack D. Neal
subfiles.about: Seeks a decision on U.S. payment for the deportation of Abe, Torigoe, and Kobayashi.
subfiles.summary: Barger weighs the cost and precedent of U.S. payment against the Embassy’s concern that the men remain a danger if released.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 713 on proposed repatriation
subfiles.from: R. M. de Lembert, U.S. Embassy, Lima
subfiles.about: Reports Peru’s response to the quoted repatriation cost and encloses Abe’s published letter.
subfiles.summary: Peru wishes to remove the men but has not agreed to pay. The despatch forwards Abe’s account of his alleged mission.

subfiles.title: La Prensa letter by Abe Kenso
subfiles.about: Abe defends his journey and denies being a terrorist.
subfiles.summary: Abe claims a Japanese government mission to Brazil, Bolivia, and Peru.

subfiles.title: Translation of Abe Kenso’s La Prensa letter
subfiles.about: English translation of Abe’s published defense of his mission.
subfiles.summary: Abe says he sought Japanese residents’ welfare and denies terrorism.

subfiles.title: Instruction no. 309 on Japanese deportees
subfiles.about: Reports that Abe and two associates are in army custody en route to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department recounts their arrest for organizing intimidation in Peru and Abe’s claims of official standing.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 766 on proposed deportation
subfiles.from: R. M. de Lembert, U.S. Embassy, Lima
subfiles.about: Considers a Peruvian police proposal to deport Abe alone using his own funds.
subfiles.summary: Peru has not committed funds for all three men. The Embassy warns that an unguarded journey could let Abe escape.

subfiles.title: Legal attaché memorandum on Abe and associates
subfiles.about: Records Inspector General Céspedes’s concern about continued detention.
subfiles.summary: Céspedes proposes prioritizing Abe’s deportation and using the money Abe holds toward travel.

subfiles.title: Airgram reporting Japanese denial of Abe’s claims
subfiles.about: Relays Japan’s finding that Abe had neither naval rank nor an official mission.
subfiles.summary: Japanese authorities found no naval record or government appointment for Abe.

subfiles.title: FBI cover letter forwarding a communication
subfiles.to: Jack D. Neal and U.S. intelligence officials
subfiles.about: Forwards a confidential source report.
subfiles.summary: Hoover circulates an attached communication to State, Navy, and War officials.

subfiles.title: FBI report on Abe’s letters and deportation
subfiles.about: Examines threatening letters, Abe’s appeals, and Peru’s effort to expel the organizers.
subfiles.summary: The report traces threatening letters sent to Japanese residents and reproduces Abe’s appeals to police, newspapers, and Peru’s president. Abe presents himself as a Japanese envoy and denies terrorism. The report also discusses Swedish Legation funds, stalled deportation arrangements, and a physical description of Abe.

subfiles.title: Telegram authorizing a U.S. cost guarantee
subfiles.about: Allows a U.S. guarantee of repatriation costs if Peru will not pay.
subfiles.summary: Authorizes the guarantee as a last resort and requests a prompt reply.

subfiles.title: Lima telegram arranging deportees’ flight
subfiles.about: Sets out the Peruvian aircraft route and custody arrangements for three deportees.
subfiles.summary: Peru will fly the men toward Miami; U.S. forces will take custody in the Canal Zone.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram reporting Japanese investigation of Abe
subfiles.about: Reports Japan’s denial of Abe’s naval service and claimed envoy role.
subfiles.summary: Japanese authorities found no basis for Abe’s claims and requested a police identity check.

subfiles.title: Lima telegram requesting flight permission
subfiles.about: Requests clearance for the Peruvian C-47 carrying the deportees.
subfiles.summary: Provides the aircraft’s route through the Canal Zone, Jamaica, Miami, San Antonio, and Washington.

subfiles.title: Record-copy replacement notice
subfiles.about: Designates an attached white copy as the record copy.
subfiles.summary: Directs return of the replacement telegram or airgram copy for filing.

subfiles.title: Telegram reporting the deportees’ departure
subfiles.about: Confirms the three Japanese left Lima by Peruvian military aircraft.
subfiles.summary: The pilot carried expulsion orders; U.S. forces were to assume custody in the Canal Zone.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 890 on deportation from Peru
subfiles.about: Forwards the legal attaché’s account of the deportees’ departure.
subfiles.summary: Reports the aircraft’s departure and planned transfer to U.S. military custody.

subfiles.title: Legal attaché report on airport transfer
subfiles.about: Describes the police escort, search, and handover of the deportees.
subfiles.summary: Peruvian police delivered the three men to Captain Gervasi’s aircraft without incident.

subfiles.title: State Department communication on repatriation
subfiles.from: Special Projects Division, Department of State
subfiles.about: Asks that the three deportees be returned from the Canal Zone to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department describes the men as dangerous organizers and leaves their eventual disposition in Japan to the Supreme Commander.

subfiles.title: Letter agreeing to transport costs
subfiles.about: Agrees to cover transport costs from the Canal Zone to Japan.
subfiles.summary: State agrees to pay for the three deportees’ transport through the United States.

subfiles.title: Tokyo airgram quoting Japanese records on Abe
subfiles.about: Forwards Japanese police records on Abe’s identity, family, work, and military status.
subfiles.summary: The records identify Abe’s birthplace and family, trace work in Osaka and Tokyo, and say he was rejected from naval service on medical grounds.

subfiles.title: FBI cover letter forwarding Aikoku Doshi Kai report
subfiles.to: Jack D. Neal and U.S. intelligence officials
subfiles.about: Forwards a confidential communication about Japanese organizers in Peru.
subfiles.summary: Hoover circulates an attached report to State, Navy, and War officials.

subfiles.title: FBI report on Aikoku Renmei documents
subfiles.about: Analyzes documents found on Abe before deportation.
subfiles.summary: The report confirms the December 1946 transfer of Abe, Kobayashi, and Torigoe to U.S. custody. It translates Aikoku Renmei propaganda, a proposed constitution, membership form, and warning letter threatening opponents with force. It also reports confiscation of Aikoku Doshi Kai membership cards.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 430 on Japanese societies, opening page
subfiles.from: Harold H. Tittmann, U.S. Embassy, Lima
subfiles.about: Introduces three Japanese associations operating in Peru.
subfiles.summary: Identifies three Lima-based societies and explains the Swedish Legation’s role in Japanese welfare affairs.

subfiles.title: Directing council of the Japanese Mutual-Cultural Association
subfiles.about: Lists the association’s officers.
subfiles.summary: A roster names members of the association’s directing council.

subfiles.title: Despatch no. 430 on Japanese societies, concluding page
subfiles.from: Harold H. Tittmann, U.S. Embassy, Lima
subfiles.about: Discusses the societies’ activities and lists enclosed records.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy describes requests to fly Japanese flags and reports that one league still claimed Japan had not lost the war.

subfiles.title: Information sheet on Sociedad Mutualista Japonesa
subfiles.about: Notes the society’s officers, seal, songs, and flag request.
subfiles.summary: Identifies Dairoku Imafuku and songs celebrating Japanese victory and punishing traitors.

subfiles.title: Invitation to Emperor’s birthday celebration
subfiles.about: Invites attendance at a youth performance and dances for the Emperor’s birthday.
subfiles.summary: Announces an April 29 event at Teatro Apolo.

subfiles.title: Duplicate copy of Emperor’s birthday invitation
subfiles.about: Repeats the invitation to the April 29 celebration.
subfiles.summary: A second, partly cropped copy of the invitation appears.

subfiles.title: Petition to fly the Japanese flag
subfiles.to: Peruvian Minister of Government and Police
subfiles.about: Requests permission to raise Japanese flags on April 29.
subfiles.summary: The society asks to display its flag for the Emperor’s birthday under Peruvian rules.

subfiles.title: Letter listing Liga de Mutualidad Japonesa officers
subfiles.about: Provides the league’s board members and mentions its registered statutes.
subfiles.summary: Koche supplies the officers’ names and says the statutes were registered.

subfiles.title: Information sheet on Liga de Mutualidad Japonesa
subfiles.about: Records the league’s address, flag circular, and police response.
subfiles.summary: Members raised flags without permission and lowered them after police intervened.

subfiles.title: Emperor’s birthday leaflet, Spanish translation
subfiles.about: Urges residents to celebrate the Emperor and fly Japanese and Peruvian flags.
subfiles.summary: The leaflet praises the Emperor and calls for an April 29 celebration.

subfiles.title: Constitution of the Japanese Mutual-Cultural Association
subfiles.doc_type: notarial constitution and statutes, opening pages
subfiles.about: Establishes the association and sets out its officers, purposes, activities, and membership rules.
subfiles.summary: The notarial instrument names the founders and records the association’s property and statutes. Its stated purposes include friendship with Peruvians, mutual aid, legal help, and assistance to Japanese residents in need. The opening rules establish Lima as its principal seat and bar participation in Peruvian party politics.
